subject: Hiring: Senior Inference Reliability - interview scope, anchors & logistics
messages:

Subject: Candidate intro: Sophie Turner - Senior Inference Reliability Engineer (resume attached)

Hi Marissa,

Quick intro: attaching Sophie Turner's resume — senior infra engineer with 7+ years (distributed systems/ML infra). Recruiter summary below.

Candidate snapshot:
- Current: Staff Infra Engineer at VertexAI Labs (focused on model serving reliability for generative workloads)
- Strengths: incident ownership, latency-sensitive system design, NVMe+GPU ops, quantization tradeoffs
- Open to: principal/staff-level roles with strong product impact

Sophie is available for a first panel the week of 6/21; she prefers mornings PT. Can you confirm:

RecruiterCo

From: marissa_cole
To: markus_klein, grace_oconnor, aditya_rao
Cc: talent@recruiterco.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate intro: Sophie Turner - Senior Inference Reliability Engineer (resume attached)

Thanks Aisha — forwarding to the core panel so we can align on scope and level. Quick notes from my side on what I'm hiring for and how I'd like the interviews to map to signals:

Role summary (what matters most):
- Ownership of production inference reliability across multi-tenant clusters (SLO design, incident playbooks, postmortems)
- Performance engineering: end-to-end latency accounting, batching strategies, KV/prefix cache tradeoffs, and cost-performance tradeoffs at scale
- Collaboration with model/ops teams: deployment gating, rollout strategies, automatic fallbacks, and model variant routing

Leveling & evaluation anchors (draft):
- System design (40%): clear tradeoffs, measurable metrics, capacity planning, and fallback strategies. Expect architecture sketches with latency/cost estimates.
- Reliability & ops (25%): incident handling examples, blameless postmortems, automation to avoid manual toil.
- Performance & kernel/infra awareness (20%): understanding of quantization, memory/KV cache management, and continuous batching implications.
- Team & mentorship (15%): cross-team influence, feedback loops, and doc/hand-off quality.

Markus — can you take bar-raiser for this loop? Focus points I'd ask you to probe: measurement-first proof, degradation-mode design, and where they drove infra-level performance wins.
Grace — could you own the hiring-manager debrief template and reserve 60-90 minutes for a combined review after the panel?
Aditya — can you run the system-design slot and add a short micro-benchmarking question (30 min)?

Attachments: I'm attaching an updated rubric (inference_role_rubric_v2.docx) and a one-pager for Sophie's candidate-facing prep. Will also send a Calendly link for a 90m loop if we decide to proceed.

If everyone agrees, I'll ask Aisha to lock availability for 6/21/6/22 mornings PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Hiring Manager, Serving & Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: inference_role_rubric_v2.docx (DOCX, 128 KB)]

From: markus_klein
To: marissa_cole, grace_oconnor, aditya_rao
Cc: talent@recruiterco.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate intro: Sophie Turner - Senior Inference Reliability Engineer (resume attached)

Marissa — happy to be bar-raiser. Read the resume quickly; a few concrete anchors I'll use during the loop:

Bar-raiser anchors (proposed)
- Measurement-first: can they define a hypothesis, choose metrics, run a small experiment, and interpret the results? Ask for a crisp example where metrics changed a design.
- Degradation modes: do they design for graceful failure? Probe fallback strategies (model variant fallback, prefix-KV pruning, token-dropping strategies), and how they tested those in prod.
- Cost-aware optimizations: tradeoffs between quantization (int8/4-bit) and accuracy, batching latency vs throughput, and when to push to cheaper VM families vs specialized GPUs.
- Postmortem discipline: ownership of a postmortem that reduced recurrence; ask for timelines and follow-through.

Logistics notes:
- I recommend a 90-minute combined panel: 30m system design (Aditya), 30m reliability/ops (Grace), 15m follow-ups, 15m buffer + break. Then a 60–90m debrief same day.
- Prep: candidate-facing one-pager is fine; also send the short micro-benchmark spec so she can be primed for that slot (not a take-home).

I'll prepare a short rubric addendum and paste it into the debrief doc during the loop so we have normalized signals.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Serving Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: panel_prep_onepager.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)]

From: marissa_cole
To: talent@recruiterco.com, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@gmail.com>
Cc: markus_klein, grace_oconnor, aditya_rao
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Sophie Turner loop and prep materials

Hi Aisha and Sophie — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per the panel's alignment:

1) We'd like to schedule a 90-minute panel on either 21 or 22 Jun, mornings PT. Sophie — are you available 6/21 9:00–10:30 AM PT or 6/22 10:00–11:30 AM PT?

2) Prep materials we'll send: candidate one-pager, short micro-benchmark spec (30-min in-session), and a PDF with the signal anchors so you know what we're focusing on. No take-home required.

3) Panel: Aditya (system design), Grace (reliability/op), Markus (bar-raiser, performance anchors), Marissa (hiring manager). We'll capture notes in the shared debrief doc (linked). Expect a 60–90 minute combined debrief after the loop; please keep calendars flexible on the same day.

Sophie — if one of the proposed times works, reply with your preferred slot and we'll lock the interview and send calendar invites.

Best,
Marissa
